metaTitle: Best Air Purifiers for Mold Spores (2026)
metaDescription: Mold air purifiers compared on spore capture, filter stages and room fit, with a plain explanation of why humidity control matters more than any filter.
expertTake: The Clorox Medium Room purifier is the top pick because it pairs a True HEPA filter with a three-stage layout and a room-size claim that fits a damp bedroom or office. The Afloia PLUTO is the value pick with a washable pre-filter and four stages. Anyone with visible mold on walls or ceilings should skip the purifier as the first step, because the growth has to be removed and the moisture source fixed.
introParagraphs: A purifier does not kill mold. It captures the spores that float in the air, which keeps them from landing and seeding new growth, but the colony itself keeps growing as long as there is moisture. Think of the machine as a way to reduce airborne spores while you fix the damp.

This guide ranks the units by how well they capture spores, which depends on filter grade and airflow, then by how they handle the damp rooms where mold lives. Spores are larger than the standard HEPA test particle, so the filter is rarely the weak link. The airflow and the room are.

products.name: Clorox Medium Room True HEPA purifier, 3-stage
products.description:
The Clorox medium-room unit is the cleanest fit for a damp room because its listing states mold among the particles it reduces and ties that to a True HEPA filter capturing 99.97 percent of particulates. Mold spores are typically a few microns across, much larger than the 0.3 micron size the HEPA standard uses, so a true HEPA layer catches them readily once they reach the filter.

The filter is a three-stage 360 degree design with a pre-filter for large particles, the HEPA layer and a carbon stage, and the 360 degree intake pulls air from around the unit. The 1,000 square foot figure is a one-change number, so a realistic mold-control room is near 200 square feet, a bedroom, a basement room or an office.

Ownership is a filter set on the maker's schedule, and Clorox keeps its replacement filters in supply. Because mold rooms are damp, check the pre-filter more often, since a damp filter can itself grow a film. Place the unit away from the wettest wall and let the air circulate. For a truly damp room, run it continuously rather than on a timer, since spores are released all day and not just when you are present.
products.bestFor: Damp bedrooms and small rooms near 200 square feet.
pros: True HEPA layer captures mold spores
Three stages with a carbon layer
Genuine filters are easy to find
cons: Does not remove the moisture source
Coverage claim is a one-change figure

products.name: Afloia PLUTO 4-stage purifier with washable pre-filter
products.description:
The PLUTO is a four-stage purifier whose listing names mold among the targets and states a 269 square foot cleaning figure, which is a more honest room size than the 1,076 square foot headline. The washable outer pre-filter is a useful feature for a damp room, because you can rinse and dry it fully to keep it from growing a film.

The four-stage layout adds a layer over a three-stage unit, and the listing describes it as imported. Compared with the Clorox, it states a smaller honest room and gives you a washable first stage, which lowers the running cost.

As a brand-claimed rating, the airflow has no third-party verification. In year three, the job is to rinse the pre-filter, dry it completely and replace the main filter on schedule, and to confirm the genuine replacement is sold before you buy. Rinsing a washable stage in a damp house has a trap: if it goes back in even slightly wet, the filter itself becomes the cleanest place for mold to settle. Dry it on a rack for a full day and keep a second pre-filter if the maker sells one, so one is always ready. The 269 square foot figure is the number to trust when you size it, and it suggests a small bedroom or a home office rather than a whole basement.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms near 270 square feet where a washable first stage is valued.
pros: States a 269 square foot cleaning figure
cons: Newer brand, so check filter supply

products.name: Clorox Medium Room Turbo True HEPA purifier

specList.label: Airflow claim
specList.value: Up to 5 air changes per hour

products.description:
The Turbo model is the Clorox for people who want faster cleaning. Its listing says the 360 degree airflow cleans medium rooms up to five times per hour, which is the allergy-grade rate and the right target for airborne spores. A turbo mode raises the fan for a quick pass after you disturb a damp corner or open a window.

The filter stack is the same three-stage design with a True HEPA layer. The difference from the standard medium unit is the extra airflow and a turbo setting, which is louder when used.

Ownership is a filter set swap, and in a damp room the pre-filter is the stage to watch. Compared with the Levoit 143 CFM tower, the Clorox is simpler and carries a specific mold claim. A practical way to use the turbo setting is to run it for twenty minutes after you vacuum or move stored boxes in a damp room, then drop back to normal. That pulls disturbed spores into the filter while they are still airborne. The five-changes-per-hour claim is the maker's figure, so allow a margin if the room is at the top of its size class.
products.bestFor: Medium damp rooms where a fast pass after disturbance is useful.
pros: States up to five air changes per hour
Turbo mode for a fast pass
cons: Does not remove the moisture source

products.name: Clorox Small Room tabletop True HEPA, 2-stage
products.description:
The small Clorox is a tabletop unit sized honestly for 200 square feet, with a True HEPA filter and a two-stage layout. A 200 square foot rating on the listing is a realistic figure, which is why it is a trustworthy buy for a small damp room such as a closet office or a bathroom-adjacent bedroom.

The filter captures 99.97 percent of allergens and particulates, which includes mold spores, and the listing reduces viruses and bacteria. With only two stages, it has less protection for the HEPA layer and no carbon bed, so it is not an odor answer for a musty room.

Ownership is simple: replace the filter on schedule. It is the cheap way to put a True HEPA filter in a damp corner. Because it is small, it works best close to where you spend time, such as a desk in a basement office, rather than across the room. Do not expect it to handle a large damp space, since its two stages and low airflow are sized for one small room. Replacing the filter on schedule matters more here than on a larger unit, because the small filter has less surface and loads sooner.
products.bestFor: Small damp rooms near 200 square feet.
pros: True HEPA at a low tier
cons: No carbon bed for musty smell

products.name: Levoit 143 CFM HEPA tower with carbon stage
products.description:
This Levoit tower brings a verified 143 CFM airflow rating, which makes it the best-documented unit here. With a stack of pre-filter, HEPA and carbon, it covers about 220 square feet at five changes per hour, which is a bedroom or a basement room.

Its carbon stage helps with the musty smell that comes with damp, though a thin sheet will not remove a deep mold odor. The 56W motor holds airflow through the filter stack.

Compared with the Clorox, it has a verified airflow figure but no mold claim on the listing. Both capture spores equally well once the air reaches the HEPA layer. In a basement room, set it on a stand a few inches off a concrete floor, since damp floors and a low intake invite moisture into the filter. Compared with the Winix 5510, it covers about half the room but costs less to run. A verified number is the reason to choose it over an unverified small unit.
products.bestFor: Basements and bedrooms near 220 square feet that need a verified rating.
pros: Genuine filters are easy to find
cons: No mold claim on the listing
Thin carbon will not cure a mold odor

products.name: Winix 5510 True HEPA, verified at 392 sq ft
products.description:
The Winix 5510 is the larger option, verified at 392 square feet with a True HEPA layer and carbon stage. For a large damp basement or a living area with a musty corner, it supplies enough airflow to keep spores moving through the filter rather than settling on surfaces.

The carbon filter targets household odors and VOCs, which helps with the musty smell. App support adds scheduling.

It is bigger and louder than the small units. In a damp room, vacuum the mesh pre-filter often. In a large damp room, place it in the middle of the longest wall and keep the mesh pre-filter clean, since a damp basement collects lint and dust that load it fast. The verified room size means you do not need to second-guess the coverage figure. It is the one pick here that suits a whole finished basement.
products.bestFor: Large damp rooms near 390 square feet.
cons: Larger and louder than the small units
Does not address the moisture source

buyingCriteria.explanation: Mold needs moisture, and keeping relative humidity between about 30 and 50 percent stops it. A purifier removes spores from the air but not the colony. Without a dehumidifier or a repaired leak, the spore count will return after the filter is saturated. Condensation on windows, a musty smell in a closed room and peeling paint near a wall are all signs that the humidity is too high.

Mold spores are typically a few microns across, much larger than the 0.3 micron HEPA test size, so a True HEPA layer captures them very well. The Clorox listings state 99.97 percent capture and mold reduction. The weak point is airflow, not the filter.

A damp basement or bathroom-adjacent bedroom needs enough airflow to turn the air over four to five times per hour. The Winix 5510's 392 square feet verified and the Levoit 143 CFM tower's 220 square feet at five changes are the honest figures.

buyingCriteria.criterion: A first stage you can dry
buyingCriteria.explanation: A damp pre-filter can grow its own film. The Afloia PLUTO's washable pre-filter is useful if you rinse it and let it dry fully. A first stage you cannot clean means a filter that stays damp.
The musty smell of mold is a gas, and only carbon addresses it. The Levoit and Winix list carbon stages, and the small Clorox has none. A thin sheet takes the edge off but does not fix a heavy smell.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Placement away from the wet wall
buyingCriteria.explanation: Do not put the unit against the wettest wall, and do not point it at a mold patch. Place it where it can draw from the middle of the room. A purifier blowing across mold can spread loose spores, so clean visible growth first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spore capture
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked each listing for a True HEPA layer and a named mold claim. The Clorox units state mold reduction, and the Afloia and Levoit list mold or dust among targets. This is a spec-sheet review.

howWeEvaluated.title: Airflow and room fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We converted coverage claims to a room using about five air changes per hour. The lineup runs from the small Clorox's 200 square feet to the Winix at 392.

howWeEvaluated.title: Damp-room design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pre-filter design and whether the first stage can be cleaned and dried. A first stage that stays damp is a weakness. Damp rooms ruin ordinary filters faster than dry ones, so this part of the review carried extra weight.

howWeEvaluated.title: Odor handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for a carbon stage. The Levoit and Winix list carbon, and the small Clorox does not.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed replacement filters and brand supply. Clorox, Levoit and Winix have established parts supply, while the Afloia is newer.

cards.label: Purifier
cards.text: The Clorox Medium Room and the Levoit tower capture spores that are already airborne. They do not lower humidity.

cards.label: Dehumidifier
cards.text: A dehumidifier removes the moisture that mold needs. For a damp room it is the first purchase, and the purifier is the second.

howToChoose.note: Buy a dehumidifier first for a damp room, and add the Clorox Medium Room or Winix 5510 to handle airborne spores.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A True HEPA layer, a pre-filter you can dry, enough airflow for four to five changes and a dehumidifier running alongside.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Levoit 143 CFM tower suits a small basement room, and the Winix 5510 suits a large one.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The room is large, or you want a verified rating, as with the Winix 5510 and the Levoit tower.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The room is small and dry enough that the small Clorox or Afloia is enough.

maintenance.why: A damp pre-filter can grow a film. Check for discoloration and a musty smell.

maintenance.why: Dry it fully before refitting. A damp filter in a damp room defeats the purpose.
A loaded medium restricts airflow and the spore capture rate falls.
A cheap hygrometer shows whether the room is staying under about 50 percent. That number matters more than the filter.
Carbon saturates and the musty smell returns.

faq.q: Will an air purifier get rid of mold?
faq.a: No. It captures airborne spores, but the colony keeps growing where there is moisture. Fix the damp and clean visible mold first. A dehumidifier, a repaired leak or better ventilation is the fix that lasts.

faq.q: Is HEPA good for mold spores?
faq.a: Yes, because spores are larger than the 0.3 micron test size. A True HEPA layer captures them very well.

faq.q: Do I also need a dehumidifier?
faq.a: For a damp room, yes. Keeping humidity between about 30 and 50 percent stops mold growing, and the purifier cannot do that. A cheap hygrometer on the shelf will tell you whether the room is staying in range.

faq.q: Are cheap purifiers fine for mold?
faq.a: If the filter is True HEPA and the room is small, yes. The small Clorox is a low-cost example.
A purifier blowing across a visible mold patch can loosen spores. Clean the growth first and place the unit away from it.
Away from the wettest wall, with a foot of clearance, in the middle of the room. Avoid placing it directly against a wall, since the intake needs room to draw.
